'''John Peter Larkindale''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|QSO|size=85%}} (born 1946) is a New Zealand former public servant and diplomat, whose overseas postings including ambassador to the Russian Federation and high commissioner to Australia.

== Biography ==
Larkindale was born in [[Wellington]] in 1946,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.worldstatesmen.org/Tokelau.html|title=Tokelau|author=Ben M. Cahoon|accessdate=30 July 2019}}</ref> to Robert and Liesel, Jewish migrants from Germany. Larkindale was educated at [[Wellington College (New Zealand)|Wellington College]].<ref name="IPANZ president">{{cite web |url=https://www.ipanz.org.nz/Story?Action=View&Story_id=43 |title=New president for IPANZ |date= |website= |publisher=Institute of Public Administration New Zealand |accessdate=30 April 2017}}</ref>  He then studied chemistry at [[Victoria University of Wellington]], graduating [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] and then [[Master of Science|MSc(Hons)]].<ref name="IPANZ president"/> His 1968 master's thesis, supervised by Alan Freeman, was titled ''Some intercalation compounds of boron nitride''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://tewaharoa.victoria.ac.nz/VUW:64VUW_ALL:64VUW_INST21136305390002386 |title=Library catalogue search |date= |website= |publisher=Victoria University of Wellington |accessdate=30 April 2017}}</ref><ref name="Halton">{{cite book |last=Halton |first=Brian |author-link=Brian Halton |title=Chemistry at Victoria – The Wellington University |url=http://www.victoria.ac.nz/scps/about/attachments/ChemHist_second-edition_lowres.pdf |accessdate=1 May 2017 |year=2014 |edition=2nd |publisher=School of Chemical & Physical Sciences, Victoria University of Wellington |isbn=978-0-475-12408-1 |page=77}}</ref> Larkindale was awarded an [[1851 Research Fellowship|1851 Exhibition Scholarship]],<ref name="Halton"/> and he went on to complete a [[PhD]] at [[McGill University]] in Canada in 1971.<ref name="IPANZ president"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://digitool.Library.McGill.CA:80/R/-?func=dbin-jump-full&object_id=70711&silo_library=GEN01 |title=Library cataglogue search |date= |website= |publisher=McGill University |accessdate=30 April 2017}}</ref> His doctoral thesis, supervised by David J. Simkin, was titled ''Spectroscopic and theoretical studies of charge-transfer complexes''.<ref>{{cite book |last=Larkindale |first=J.P. |author-link=John Larkindale |title=Spectroscopic and theoretical studies of charge-transfer complexes |url=http://digitool.library.mcgill.ca/webclient/DeliveryManager?pid=70711 |accessdate=30 April 2017 |year=1971 |publisher=McGill University |location=Montreal}}</ref>

Larkindale joined the staff of the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (New Zealand)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] in 1972, and had postings to New Zealand's embassies in Vienna and Washington. He then served as the director of Pacific aid, based in Wellington and, later, [[Tokelau]] official secretary.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}} Subsequently, he was the deputy head of mission in Beijing and then London. In 1994, he was appointed executive director of the Commonwealth Heads of Government (CHOGM) task force, responsible for organising the [[Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 1995|CHOGM summit]] held in [[Auckland]] the following year.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}}

In the [[1996 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|1996 New Year Honours]], Larkindale was appointed a [[Companion of the Queen's Service Order]] for public services.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=54256 |date=30 December 1995 |page=34 |supp=2}}</ref>

Between 1996 and 1999, Larkindale was the [[List of ambassadors of New Zealand to Russia|New Zealand ambassador to the Russian Federation]]. Returning to Wellington, he was appointed deputy secretary of the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (New Zealand)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade]]. Larkindale's final diplomatic appointment was as [[List of High Commissioners of New Zealand to Australia|high commissioner to Australia]], in which role he served from 2006 until his retirement in 2011.<ref name="IPANZ president"/>

Larkindale became a member of the board of the [[Institute of Public Administration New Zealand]] (IPANZ) in 2012, and in March 2013 he was elected president of IPANZ.<ref name="IPANZ president"/>
